pr.title: feat(api): add internal PCP referral CRUD endpoints

decisions.title: Admit null on the enum stage fields via anyOf, not type+enum+nullable
decisions.chose: Use `anyOf: [ $ref LeadStage, { type: null } ]` for therapyLeadStage/psychLeadStage on the update request; keep `nullable: true` for the 10 nullable string fields.
decisions.rejected: `type:string + enum + nullable:true` (compiles clean under strict mode but silently refuses null — the trap), and `allOf + nullable` (fails route registration outright).
decisions.why: Spiked all five candidate forms against ajv@8.18.0 with the server's actual options; only null-in-type, null-in-enum, and anyOf actually admit null. anyOf avoids putting null inside an enum, which would trip the repo's Spectral SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE rule. The generated TypeScript looked correct the whole time, so type-checking alone would not have caught the trap — the route simply would not register.

decisions.title: Reject an unfiltered referral list with 422 — filters are a type-level union
decisions.chose: `ReferralListFilters` is a union of the four indexed filter shapes; a filterless service call is a type error, and the route returns 422.
decisions.rejected: A scan-and-filter fallback, or the non-null assertion my first draft used.
decisions.why: Referrals carry PHI and the four GSI lookups cover every operator use case, so there is no scan to fall back to. Modeling filters as a union makes 'no filter' unrepresentable rather than a runtime surprise.

decisions.title: Create validation mirrors PcpReferralRow's constraints
decisions.chose: The create request enforces the same constraints as the stored PcpReferralRow (settling plan §7 with 'same validation').
decisions.rejected: Looser create input for test-fixture convenience.
decisions.why: Looser input invites fixtures the batch pipeline can't process; matching the row's constraints keeps every created referral batch-valid.

decisions.title: Assert GSI4 case-sensitivity in both directions (referringProviderId)
decisions.chose: Provider-id lookup is case-sensitive (GSI4 `casing:none`) while name/practice/referrer lookups upper-case; the test asserts a wrong-case provider id returns nothing, not just that the right case works.
decisions.why: GSI1/2/3 use `casing:upper` but GSI4 is `casing:none` — a one-directional test would still pass if that asymmetry regressed.

decisions.title: Leave delete-all and upsertReferral untouched (deliberate non-change)
decisions.chose: `DELETE /internal/pcp-referrals` (delete-all) keeps its path, operationId, and 204; `upsertReferral`'s Hex-ingest semantics are untouched.
decisions.rejected: Folding delete-one and delete-all together, or changing ingest.
decisions.why: Both are relied on elsewhere and out of scope: the ingest path feeds the batch, and the delete-all contract is already published. Changing either here would add risk for no in-scope benefit.

decisions.title: A referral patch touches only submitted fields — asserted on the whole object
decisions.chose: `updateReferral` applies only the submitted fields; the test compares the entire stored record against the created one.
decisions.rejected: Field-by-field assertions that could miss a collateral change.
decisions.why: Referrals carry 12 optional fields; a patch that disturbed mobile/email/networkName/insuranceCarrier must fail loudly. Mutation-checked: making updateReferral wipe an omitted field fails exactly this whole-object test.
